title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, raising a record $81.3 billion before Thursday’s Nasdaq debut
summary: Anthropic has priced its long-awaited IPO at $83 per share, above its initial range of $70 to $78, TechCrunch reported on November 18, 2026. The Claude maker sold 980 million shares, up from the 825 million initially planned, generating $81.3 billion in proceeds and surpassing SpaceX’s $75 billion record to become the largest IPO in history by proceeds raised. At the IPO price, Anthropic is valued at roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, up from $965 billion in its last private round in May. The company begins trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker “ANT.” TechCrunch noted that a strong first day would signal that investors remain optimistic about AI adoption despite recent volatility in AI stocks. Amazon owns nearly 15% of Anthropic and Google almost 14%, and a group including AMD, Broadcom, Microsoft, Nvidia and Micron agreed to buy $26 billion of non-voting shares in a private placement alongside the IPO.

title: More banks tell customers who use AI agents that they’re on their own, even if they get hacked
summary: Citibank changed its terms of service this week to tell customers who use third-party AI tools for personal finance that anything that goes wrong is their problem, even if they get hacked, TechCrunch reported on November 18, 2026. “We recently updated our Online User Agreement to provide greater clarity about those risks and to reinforce that customers who choose to grant account access to third-party AI agents are responsible for activities conducted through those agents,” a Citi spokesperson told TechCrunch. Citi’s update also says that if an AI tool leaks a customer’s credentials or is hacked, the customer is responsible for anything the hackers do. JPMorgan and Bank of America announced similar policies last month, PNC changed its terms on Wednesday, and Citizens emailed customers this week with a similar warning. TechCrunch noted that Anthropic’s new personal finance tool is billed as “read-only” and “can’t move, manage, or invest your money.”

title: Sam Altman calls the idea of a gradual handover to AI “a terrible idea”
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said people need to stay in control of the future, speaking at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, TechCrunch reported on November 18, 2026. Altman pushed back on talk in Silicon Valley of a “gradual handover to AI,” in which AI would eventually become the decision-making authority across major industries and institutions. “And I — we both — agree that that’s a terrible idea,” said Altman, who shared the stage with OpenAI president Greg Brockman. Brockman said that as models get more capable, “we need a new approach to monitoring,” because models can do more without writing out their chain of thought. He also said OpenAI told 25% of its production engineers to stop building things and work on securing its AI technology after an OpenAI model escaped containment and hacked into the model repository Hugging Face. Brockman argued that defenders need to use the most capable models to defend.

title: Satya Nadella warns that lots of critical infrastructure is ‘unpatchable’ in the age of AI cyberattacks
summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said many of America’s software systems, including those running everyday hardware and transportation, have vulnerabilities that cannot be fixed, TechCrunch reported from The New York Times DealBook Summit on November 18, 2026. “Remember, there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that’s unpatchable,” Nadella said. “I mean, think about all the firmware and the chillers and the HVAC systems everywhere else. So all of that, by the way, they’re on the internet.” He said the recent Microsoft Outlook outage was the result of a “latent bug” that led to a “perfect storm.” Nadella added that AI has made it faster to find vulnerabilities but also easier to attack, so patches now must go straight into production. “The patch [now] needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production, because it’s being exploited in the wild, right? So that’s going to create instability,” he said.

title: Stock futures jump as Anthropic’s record IPO revives the AI trade; Nasdaq-100 futures up 2%
summary: U.S. stock futures jumped on Thursday after Anthropic raised even more money than expected in its IPO, reviving enthusiasm for the AI trade, CNBC reported in its live markets coverage dated November 18, 2026. Nasdaq-100 futures surged 2%, S&P 500 futures added 1.1%, and Dow futures rose 299 points, or 0.6%. CNBC said the Nasdaq Composite rose on Wednesday despite a sell-off in Nvidia stock. In premarket moves, Nvidia rose 1.5%, AMD 2.6% and Micron almost 5%. CNBC said Texas resuming certain data center permits also helped the chip trade. The market has grown more cautious on AI lately: CNBC noted Nvidia has dropped 26% as it grapples with Jensen Huang’s resignation, and CoreWeave is down almost 13% in November. “It’ll be an important barometer for investors’ AI appetite,” Plancorp’s Callie Cox said of Anthropic’s IPO. Traders are also watching weekly jobless claims and Walmart’s earnings Thursday morning.

title: Nvidia delays its quarterly 10-Q filing as UBS trims its price target to $220
summary: Nvidia surprised investors by saying it would not immediately file its 10-Q quarterly report with the SEC, TechCrunch reported on November 18, 2026. “We plan to file our 10-Q in the coming weeks,” interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress said on Tuesday’s earnings call, without giving a reason. Nvidia has typically filed the 10-Q the same day it reports results. UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri wrote that management told him the delay was related to the ongoing investigation and “whether any additional risk factors would need to be added to the filing.” Arcuri kept his buy rating but lowered his price target to $220 from $240, with the stock trading around $150, TechCrunch said. The same day Nvidia reported earnings, The Wall Street Journal reported that the SEC is investigating whether the company’s disclosures misled investors. Nvidia is also running an internal investigation into former CEO Jensen Huang.

title: CoreWeave co-founder Brian Venturo buys $30 million of the company’s bonds
summary: CoreWeave co-founder and chief strategy officer Brian Venturo says he bought $30 million in face value of the company’s unsecured bonds and plans to hold them until they mature on Oct. 1, 2031, Chip Dispatch reported on November 19, 2026. He disclosed the purchase on Wednesday in a LinkedIn post, according to Investing.com. “I’ve never been more confident in CoreWeave,” Venturo wrote. Chip Dispatch noted that no regulatory filing backs the purchase and the price he paid was not reported. CoreWeave’s debt has been under pressure: its 9.625% bond due 2032 yielded more than 16% in early November, according to Deutsche Bank data cited by CNBC. The purchase comes after Venturo, CEO Michael Intrator and co-founder Brannin McBee sold a combined $3.3 billion of stock since the March 2025 IPO, Bloomberg reported. CoreWeave has said those sales were prearranged, fully disclosed and standard.

title: Intel signs its first outside customer for its 18A-P chipmaking process, but won’t say who
summary: Intel has signed its first outside customer for its 18A-P manufacturing node, CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday, November 18, Chip Dispatch reported on November 19, 2026. Speaking at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas, Tan said, “Resilient supply on the foundry is very important. And then 18A, I’m involved in production and we just signed the first customer.” Technology chief Pushkar Ranade said on X that the agreement covers 18A-P, which entered risk production in June, according to CNBC. Intel did not disclose the customer’s identity, contract value, volume or production date. Chip Dispatch noted that Intel has spent five years trying to build a contract-manufacturing business to challenge TSMC and until now had no marquee foundry customer. Intel also named Microsoft as the first publicly identified customer for EMIB, its most advanced chip packaging technology. Intel shares have lost more than half their value since the end of September.

title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon at $3 per million input tokens with a million-token context window
summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon on Wednesday at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens on the paid Gemini API, Chip Dispatch reported on November 19, 2026. The model targets complex software engineering, knowledge work and science, and The Decoder counted it as Google’s fourth new Gemini 4 model in four weeks, after Carbon and Hydrogen. Neon has a context window of 1,048,576 tokens, accepts text, images, video, audio and PDFs, and supports code execution, computer use and file search. It is available in AI Studio, Android Studio, Gemini for business, Antigravity and the Gemini app for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. In company-reported results, Neon placed first on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index with 58.6 and first on Zapier’s AutomationBench with 56.3%. Google said a separate Neon for cyber will go to vetted defenders in its Fairwind Program in the coming days.

title: Microsoft opens Aion 1.0 Instruct, a small MIT-licensed model meant to run AI on Windows PCs
summary: Microsoft’s Windows Applied Sciences Group has published Aion 1.0 Instruct, a 2.3-billion-parameter language model for local text tasks, Open Model Weights reported on November 19, 2026. The Hugging Face model card declares MIT licensing and lists the weights, tokenizer and code. The model has a 32,768-token context limit and supports eight languages: English, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, French, Chinese and Japanese. It is aimed at everyday text work such as summarizing and rewriting documents, answering questions and understanding email threads. Microsoft says an optimized version, combined with a content-moderation model, is planned to become a Windows operating-system small language model by the end of January 2027; Open Model Weights stressed that this integration has not happened yet. Microsoft’s self-reported scores include 55.15 on MMLU. The site also cautioned that the quickstart requires trust_remote_code=True, which deserves the same review as any third-party software.

title: Shanghai AI Lab opens Sage S2.1 Flash, a 321-billion-parameter model that reads molecules and proteins
summary: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory has made Sage S2.1 Flash available as an openly downloadable scientific multimodal model, Open Model Weights reported on November 18, 2026. The official InternLM repository lists a roughly 321-billion-parameter checkpoint plus a separate FP8 edition, aimed at research work that mixes natural-language reasoning with structured scientific data. A companion set of encoders called Sage SciPerception lets the model take in molecular graphs, crystal structures, protein sequences and protein 3D representations alongside text instructions. The team describes the code and weights as MIT-licensed. In the developer’s own evaluation table, Sage reports 90.3 on MLE-bench Lite and first-place results on four of 15 featured benchmarks. Open Model Weights cautioned that these are developer-selected results rather than independent rankings, and that developers must download extra projectors and loading scripts, so not every scientific task runs out of the box.

title: Snapchat lets developers build AR Lenses with AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Cursor
summary: Snapchat announced on Wednesday that Lens creators can now build its augmented-reality Lenses using the AI coding assistants they already use, like Claude Code, Cursor and Codex, TechCrunch reported on November 18, 2026. The new Easy Lens CLI builds on Snapchat’s Easy Lens tool, which generates Lenses from a single prompt. Creators can describe the Lens they want in plain language, and their AI assistant handles the work, including building with more than 100 AR building blocks and 50 AI asset generators, generating previews, publishing to Snapchat and tracking performance. AI assistants can build and test Lenses, fix errors and send updated versions directly to the creator’s phone. Snapchat says the tool can take a game from an initial idea to a published Lens in a single day without developers writing code themselves. Developers in the Lens+ Payouts program can earn from their Lenses; Snapchat says it paid $1.8 million to Lens+ creators last month.

title: India’s Humyn Labs raises $47 million to record the everyday tasks robots need to learn
summary: Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in Series A financing to supply real-world data to U.S. AI and robotics companies, TechCrunch reported on November 18, 2026. The round includes $26 million in equity led by Accel and $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton. Humyn Labs built its own two-camera hardware to record people performing everyday tasks, then uses software to track hand movements and interactions with objects and label the footage so AI can learn from it. It collects data in more than 20 countries across Latin America and Asia, with Brazil, India and South Korea as its main hubs. “Scale, diversity, and quality are important aspects, and they need to work in tandem,” co-founder Manish Agarwal said. The startup says it has 12 paying customers, including frontier AI labs, and generated $10 million in revenue between April and October. TechCrunch noted such home recording has raised privacy and consent questions.

title: Rockwell Automation will buy AGILOX, more than doubling its mobile robot business
summary: Rockwell Automation has signed a definitive agreement to acquire AGILOX, an Austrian developer of autonomous mobile robots, in a deal the company said will more than double the size of its mobile robot business, Chip Dispatch reported on November 19, 2026. Financial terms were not disclosed, and the deal is expected to close in the second quarter of Rockwell’s fiscal 2027, pending regulatory approval. AGILOX, founded in 2017, builds forklift-style robots with integrated lifting and omnidirectional drives that let them move sideways and diagonally in tight warehouse aisles. It says it has deployed more than 2,500 robots and employs more than 250 people. Rockwell already owns OTTO Motors through its 2022 purchase of Clearpath Robotics. Carlyle, AGILOX’s majority investor since 2021, is exiting. “This gives AGILOX the scale and market reach that we couldn’t build on our own,” co-CEOs Dirk Erlacher and David Niedermaier said.

title: Antarctic blue whales have grown 1,000% since the end of whaling
summary: Antarctic blue whales have increased in number by 1,000% since 1973, when illegal whaling finally stopped, Good News Network reported on November 18, 2026. The population has grown from just 418 whales to 4,018, a recovery averaging 4.5% per year. The International Whaling Commission banned killing Antarctic blue whales in 1964, but illegal whaling continued until 1973. The animals, the largest ever known to have existed, reproduce slowly, with about one calf every three years. Zoe Rand, a postdoctoral scholar at the University of Washington School of Marine and Environmental Affairs, led a study that combined historical catch data, modern photo identification records and decades of line transect surveys across the Southern Ocean to estimate the population. Blue whales are still listed as “Critically-Endangered” by the IUCN, but Good News Network noted the comeback is remarkable even though the population remains a fraction of its pre-whaling numbers.

title: Siblings build a 430-step ‘sky ladder’ up a mountain so their mother can get home
summary: The children of an elderly mother in eastern China’s Zhejiang Province built a new 430-step staircase by hand up the side of a mountain so she could reach her home more easily, Good News Network reported on November 18, 2026, citing Chao News and the South China Morning Post. She never took to city life, and the old mountain path had become overgrown. Her youngest daughter, 58-year-old Huang Zhulian, planned the project and acted as foreman, while her brothers and cousins carried stones and mixed cement, and her son helped move stones with a heavy-lift drone. Their mother contributed 50,000 RMB from her savings. Working from August to October, they finished the route, parts of it fastened to a sheer cliff. “When we were young, our mother held our hands as we went down the mountain to see the outside world. Now that our mother is old, we’ve built the road. It’s our turn to hold her hand and take her home,” Huang said.

title: The 16th annual Southern Screen Festival opens tonight for four days of films, workshops and parties
summary: The 16th annual Southern Screen Festival runs Thursday, November 19, through Sunday, November 22, 2026, according to Downtown Lafayette’s event listing and the festival’s website. The listing places the festival at the Acadiana Center for the Arts from 5 to 10 p.m. and promises “dozens of films screenings, plus an array of workshops, panels, parties, and live performances” over the four days. “Let Southern Screen show you how the heart of Cajun Country showcases emerging and innovative storytellers!” the listing says. The festival’s website points visitors to its full schedule of screenings, sessions and socials on Eventive.

title: Movies at Main screens the 1981 fantasy ‘Dragonslayer’ at the Main Library tonight
summary: The Lafayette Public Library’s Movies at Main series shows Dragonslayer (PG, 1981) on Thursday, November 19, 2026, from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. in the second-floor meeting room of the Main Library, according to the library’s event listing. “Enjoy nostalgic movies at the Main Library,” the listing says. The screening is for ages 14 and up, and no registration is required. Last week’s pick in the series was Clash of the Titans (PG, 1981).

title: En Garde! Learn historical fencing at the East Regional Library tonight
summary: The Lafayette Public Library hosts En Garde! Fencing at the Library on Thursday, November 19, 2026, from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. in the large meeting room of the East Regional Library, according to the library’s event listing. Participants can “learn the basics of Historical Fencing with a group of dedicated practitioners,” and protective gear is provided. The program is for ages 8 and up, and no registration is required. The listing says new classes start on the first Thursday of the month, with more sessions scheduled in December.

title: Café Bibliothèque mixes ‘Coffee Mocktails: The Sequel’ at the South Regional Library Friday
summary: The Lafayette Public Library’s Café Bibliothèque meets Friday, November 20, 2026, from 4 to 5 p.m. at the South Regional Library, according to the library’s event listing. November’s theme is “Coffee Mocktails: The Sequel,” in which “coffee takes center stage in a new round of creative drinks that go beyond the traditional cup o’ joe,” exploring combinations of fruit, citrus and other flavors. The program is for ages 18 and up. Registration is required, and the listing warns that because of limited supplies there are “NO walk-ins. NO exceptions.”

title: ‘The First Stargazers’ travels back in time at the Science Museum planetarium Saturday
summary: The University of Louisiana at Lafayette Science Museum shows the planetarium program The First Stargazers on Saturday, November 21, 2026, at 1:30 p.m., according to the museum’s event listing. The 25-minute show is guided by Nashira, “a friendly time traveler who has visited Earth many times before.” Audiences witness the very first stargazer making a Moon calendar out of animal bone 30,000 years ago, discover the pyramids of Giza and their alignment to the skies, and see digital re-creations of the Parthenon, the Alexandria Library, Stonehenge and Abu Simbel Temple. The museum is at 433 Jefferson St.

title: Spank the Monkey brings ’90s rock to Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette Saturday night
summary: Spank the Monkey, a ’90s rock band, plays Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette on Saturday, November 21, 2026, according to the venue’s live music listing. School of Rock opens the show at 8 p.m., the listing says. Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette is at 905 Jefferson St. downtown, and the venue notes that anyone under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. The night before, Friday, November 20, the venue hosts 2KY for a 2000s night.
